notesStmt.note: Horace Traubel's notes for his visit to Whitman on 10 June 1889 suggest that a final draft of this poem had been completed by that date, as he mentions that a letter addressed to James Gordon Bennett, editor of the New York Herald, lay on the table and that it contained "a poemet—a little conceit—suggested by the Exposition." (See With Walt Whitman in Camden [Carbondale: Southern Illinois University Press, 1964] 5:280).
"Bravo, Paris Exposition!" was first published in Harper's Weekly on 28 September 1889 and reprinted, with a few changes in punctuation, in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

lg.l: Add to your show, dear France,

With all the rest, temples, machines,
ores, ‸goods, the visible concrete,
America's applause, love, ‸memories and good will

Sent A sentiment, sent over sea, in wafted from many
million ‸heart throbs, from

From fifty Nations and nebulous
Nations, here united,

The We grandsons and great grandsons, do not
forget your grand-sires and great grand-sires.)
